headline: Do not form or use out-of-bounds pointers or array subscripts
description: Ensure pointer arithmetic and array indexing stay within valid object boundaries to prevent memory corruption and potential code execution vulnerabilities.
automotive_rationale: In ECU communication gateways (UDS diagnostic services, CAN-FD message parsers), malicious or malformed packets from OBD-II ports can trigger out-of-bounds buffer writes, overwriting critical control parameters or RTOS return addresses.
asil_level_impact: ISO 21434 Cybersecurity Threat Level: Critical / ASIL-D.
cwe_mapping: CWE-119 (Improper Restriction of Operations within the Bounds of a Memory Buffer), CWE-121 (Stack-based Buffer Overflow)
non_compliant_example: memcpy(rx_frame.data, raw_buf, pdu_len); /* pdu_len is untrusted input from CAN bus without upper bound check */
remediation: Enforce strict length validation against sizeof target buffer before any memory copy operation.

headline: Ensure that integer conversions do not result in lost or misinterpreted data
description: Converting an integer to another type with a different width or signedness can result in truncation, sign change, or overflow.
automotive_rationale: Vehicle sensor readings (vehicle speed, motor RPM, steering angle) frequently convert between signed 32-bit CAN signals and 16-bit ECU control registers. Truncation can invert negative values or saturate motor controllers unexpectedly.
asil_level_impact: ASIL-C (Severe unintended motor acceleration or regenerative brake cutoff).
cwe_mapping: CWE-197 (Numeric Truncation Error), CWE-190 (Integer Overflow or Wraparound)
non_compliant_example: uint16_t actuator_cmd = (uint16_t)target_rpm; /* Truncation if target_rpm exceeds 65535 */
remediation: Perform explicit value-range validation before downcasting integers to narrower types.

headline: Avoid race conditions when accessing shared objects between threads and ISRs
description: Shared global variables modified in Interrupt Service Routines (ISRs) and read in task contexts must use atomic access or enter critical sections.
automotive_rationale: In ECU firmware, high-priority CAN RX interrupt handlers write to shared ring buffers while lower-priority 10ms periodic control tasks read from them. Unsynchronized access causes race conditions and corrupted vehicle state matrices.
asil_level_impact: ASIL-D (Non-deterministic vehicle telemetry causing sporadic safety interlock triggers).
cwe_mapping: CWE-362 (Concurrent Execution using Shared Resource with Improper Synchronization)
non_compliant_example: uint16_t current_val = g_can_mailbox_counter; /* Race condition if ISR interrupts read mid-word */
remediation: Wrap shared object accesses in AUTOSAR SuspendAllInterrupts()/ResumeAllInterrupts() or use C11 atomic primitives.

headline: Do not dereference null pointers
description: Ensure pointer validity before dereferencing to prevent hard fault exceptions and system crashes.
automotive_rationale: Passing null pointers across AUTOSAR Run-Time Environment (RTE) ports or device driver callbacks triggers ARM Cortex-M Memory Management Fault (MemManage / HardFault), resulting in immediate ECU reboot during driving.
asil_level_impact: ASIL-D (Sudden ECU reset leading to loss of power steering or brake assist).
non_compliant_example: reg_val = p_config->baud_rate; /* Dereference without checking for NULL */
remediation: Add defensive null-check guards at the start of all public API functions and driver entry points.

headline: Only free memory allocated dynamically
description: Attempting to free memory allocated statically or on the stack results in undefined behavior and memory allocator corruption.
automotive_rationale: Corrupting the internal memory structures can allow attackers to hijack control flow via stack manipulation.
cwe_mapping: CWE-590 (Free of Memory not on the Heap)
compliant_example: /* Use strictly static buffers and avoid calling free() */
non_compliant_example:
char local_buf[64];
free(local_buf); /* Attempt to free stack memory */
remediation: Do not call free on statically declared buffers or stack variables.
